Name: Increasing fees charged to buildings not discharged from the alternative enforcement program within the first four months of an initial notice.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to increasing fees charged to buildings not discharged from the alternative enforcement program within the first four months of an initial notice

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Housing and Buildings

Summary: This bill would increase fees charged to certain buildings participating in the Department of Housing Preservation’s Alternative Enforcement Program which have not been discharged from such program within the first four months of an initial notice of participation to the owner of such building’s participation in such program.
Text:
Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subdivision p of section 27-2153 of title 27 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended to read as follows:
p. An owner of a building who has been notified of participation in the alternative enforcement program pursuant to subdivision g of this section shall be subject to fees for any inspection, reinspection or any other action taken by the department in relation to such building during the time period that the building is in such program. A schedule of fees for this purpose shall be prescribed in rules promulgated by the department, and shall include the following: 
(i) For a building-wide inspection, monitoring of repair work and reassessment of a building conducted pursuant to subdivisions k and m of this section, the owner of any such building shall be subject to fees of at least $1,000 per dwelling unit every six months, beginning on the date of the building-wide inspection, with a maximum total fee of at least $2,000 per dwelling unit during participation in the alternative enforcement program; 
(ii) For each inspection based upon a complaint that results in issuance of a class b or class c violation, the owner of any such building shall be subject to a fee of at least $500 per inspection;
(iii) For each reinspection pursuant to a certification of correction of violation(s) submitted to the department, where the department finds that one or more violations have not been corrected, the owner of any such building shall be subject to a fee of at least $150 per reinspection per building. 
§ 2. This local law takes effect 180 days after becoming law.
